stories.title: The British island where red squirrels are thriving
summary: Conservationists say that, with red squirrels dwindling in the UK, Jersey is an "important refuge".

stories.title: Northern Ireland needs 'courage and leadership' to tackle climate change
summary: The new chair of the Climate Change Committee is spending two days in Northern Ireland on a fact-finding mission.

stories.title: Capybara pups at Manx zoo draw record crowds
summary: Curraghs Wildlife Park has its busiest October weekend ever after the birth of eight capybara pups.

stories.title: Volunteers help save one of London's rarest plants
summary: Tower mustard has suffered steep decline in London but has been successfully grown and replanted.

stories.title: Alaska’s monster tsunami sent water 1,580 feet up a mountain
summary: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area.
Scientists discovered that the disaster was preceded by several warning signs, including rapid glacier retreat, heavy rainfall, and thousands of tiny seismic tremors.
As glaciers retreat, similar disasters could become a growing danger in mountainous coastal regions.

stories.title: Why some people escape Alzheimer’s despite carrying a high-risk gene
summary: Scientists have discovered why some people with a high genetic risk of Alzheimer’s remain mentally sharp into their 80s, uncovering a rare mutation that protects the brain from harmful protein buildup.
The findings reveal a potential new way to prevent early brain damage and could pave the way for treatments that mimic this natural defense.

stories.title: Something strange is happening beneath a volcano near 2 million people
summary: Scientists have discovered evidence of two hidden magma sources beneath Nicaragua’s Masaya volcano, where satellite observations revealed mysterious ground movements suggesting magma is shifting deep underground.
The findings could improve eruption forecasting for the active volcano, which sits near 2 million people and attracts tourists to its spectacular lava lake.

stories.title: Just 3,000 steps a day may help slow Alzheimer's, scientists find
summary: Walking just 3,000 steps a day could help slow Alzheimer’s-related brain changes, according to new research.

Scientists discovered that physical activity was linked to less buildup of harmful tau proteins and nearly half the cognitive and functional decline, even in people already showing early signs of the disease.
The strongest benefits appeared at 5,000 to 7,500 daily steps, suggesting that the popular 10,000-step goal may not be necessary.

stories.title: A simple touch can bring dying corals back to life in just 7 weeks
summary: Scientists have discovered that severely bleached corals can make a remarkable comeback simply by touching healthy, genetically identical corals.
In laboratory experiments, dying corals regained their color and fully recovered within seven weeks, with as little as five days of contact sometimes enough to start the healing process.

stories.title: Astronomers discover a ghostly green star unlike any known before
summary: Astronomers have uncovered a surprising rainbow of dead stars, including the first known star that would appear genuinely green to human eyes.
Researchers found that white dwarfs can glow in unexpected shades of pink, purple, yellow, and cyan because of unusual chemical interactions in their extremely dense atmospheres.

stories.title: Scientists win 2026 Nobel Prize for controlling brain cells with light
summary: A discovery in tiny algae led to a Nobel Prize-winning breakthrough that allows scientists to switch brain cells on and off using light.
The revolutionary technique has already helped researchers activate memories and is opening new possibilities for restoring vision and treating brain disorders.

stories.title: "Mind-blowing" Alzheimer’s breakthrough: Two hours of sleep restored without clearing brain plaques
summary: Scientists have uncovered an unexpected culprit behind sleep loss in Alzheimer’s disease: overactive immune cells in the brain.
By temporarily removing these cells, researchers restored more than two hours of sleep per day in mice, revealing a promising new target for treatment.

stories.title: Volunteers plant 109,000 trees in new woodlands
summary: In the last two seasons, almost 500,000 trees and 27,233 metres of new hedges, have been planted.

stories.title: Fatty liver disease is actually five different conditions, scientists discover
summary: A common liver disease affecting nearly 30% of adults worldwide may be far more complicated than scientists previously realized.

Mayo Clinic researchers have discovered that fatty liver disease actually consists of five distinct biological subtypes, each carrying different risks for liver failure, cancer, heart disease, and other serious complications.

stories.title: BBC visits wildfire front in haze-choked Indonesia
summary: The BBC is in central Kalimantan, where a toxic haze fuelled by wildfires is choking millions of residents.

stories.title: Modern neuroscience is rediscovering a surprising idea freud had 130 years ago
summary: Researchers have identified striking parallels between Sigmund Freud’s century-old theories and modern neuroscience, suggesting that the brain’s constant predictions shape how we experience reality.
The findings could help explain why harmful thought patterns are so difficult to break and offer new insights into treating mental disorders.

stories.title: Fears for protected bats if glamping pod plans are approved
summary: Without a mitigation strategy the effect on the creatures would be "major", a survey says.

stories.title: Fuel leak spreads more than two miles along River Taff
summary: Public Health Wales advises people living nearby to shut their doors and windows due to the smell.
